To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is a static optimal external memory data structure that uses O(1/B) pages to answer queries and uses O(1) pages to update the data structure; 2) there is a self-adjusting data structure that answers a sequence of queries with a total cost of O(n/B) I/Os, where n is the total number of items; 3) there are no static optimal data structures that answer a sequence of queries using less than O(n/B) pages

(1) a static dictionary data structure for external memory string data is optimal, (2) the static data structure is optimal for dynamic string data, and (3) the data structure is optimal even when the data is not static and dynamic but is a sequence of random strings.
• We prove that a dictionary data structure for string data, which is optimal in terms of I/Os, is also optimal in terms of internal memory accesses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of self-adjusting string data structures that are optimal in the external memory setting.
the design and analysis of data structures for string dictionaries in external memory.
the following questions: What is the best possible self-adjusting data structure in external memory? How can we achieve it? We answer the above questions in this dissertation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in external memory model, a dictionary data structure that achieves optimal worst-case I/Os for a sequence of string operations is the one that is self-adjusting and uses a fixed number of B-way merging and splitting steps per string operation.
, for any string dictionary operation, there is a data structure that performs a constant number of I/Os per operation, and the data structure can be constructed in linear time.
we provide a static optimality theorem for string dictionary operations in the external memory string access model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prove a static optimality theorem for string access.
we provide a static optimality theorem for string dictionary operations in the external memory setting.
, for any constant B, we can construct a self-adjusting data structure that supports dictionary operations in O(1) I/Os.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the external memory model can be used as an abstraction to study self-adjusting string data structures, and that the external memory string dictionary problem can be efficiently solved by a static data structure that uses a single string as an index.
, in this model, a data structure that achieves optimal I/Os is static.

, for the external memory model, the static optimality theorem holds, i.e., the optimal I/O bound of a self-adjusting data structure is the optimal I/O of a non-self-adjusting data structure, up to a constant factor.
